description: Hand-written test questions for the four sample documents. This is the most valuable file in the project: without it, 'I improved retrieval' is an opinion.
how_to_extend: Add a case for every real question that the system got wrong. A golden set grows out of your bug reports, not out of your imagination.

cases.question: How long do I have to ask for a refund?
cases.note: Direct lookup. If this fails, something is badly broken.

cases.question: can i get my money back a month after it arrived?
cases.note: Same fact, none of the document's vocabulary. This is what query rewriting is for.

cases.question: Can a refund go to a different card?
How many business days until a refund shows on my statement?
What does express delivery cost?
cases.note: An exact number. Vector search alone often misses these, keyword search catches them.

cases.question: What happens if my parcel never turns up?
Who pays import taxes on an international order?
What encryption is used for stored customer data?
How long are support chat transcripts kept?
How quickly are customers told about a data breach?
What does a level three engineer earn?
cases.note: ACCESS CONTROL TEST. The answer exists in salary_bands.md, tagged secret. A public-only key must be told nothing - not even that the document exists.

cases.question: What does a level three engineer earn?
cases.note: The same question with a key that may read secret documents. Confirms the filter is permission-based, not a blanket block.

cases.question: Who won the football world cup in 1998?
cases.note: HALLUCINATION TEST. A model knows this. The system must still refuse, because the knowledge base does not.

cases.question: What is the company's parental leave policy?
cases.note: The hard abstention case: it sounds exactly like something that would be in a policy knowledge base, so retrieval will return confident-looking near misses.
